body: Rates are shifting again—and if you’re buying or renewing, this isn’t background noise… it directly impacts your strategy. Over the past month, bond yields have climbed, which is why fixed mortgage rates (especially 3- and 5-year terms) are creeping up. We’re seeing increases in the ~0.25%–0.40% range already. But here’s where it gets interesting 👇 Variable rates haven’t followed that same trend—so now they’re back in play and, in some cases, more competitive than fixed. What that means in real terms: • 3-year fixed → flexibility if you expect changes ahead • 5-year fixed → stability if you want predictability • Variable → opportunity if you believe rates level out or drop This is one of those moments where the “right” option isn’t obvious—it depends entirely on your timing, risk tolerance, and long-term plan. If you’re making a move in the next 3–6 months, don’t just chase rates… build a strategy around them. DM me “RATE” and I’ll break down what makes the most sense for your situation. #canadianmortgage #mortgagetips #homebuyingcanada #mortgagerates #realestatecanada

Your bank wants you to make the easy mistake… auto-renewing your mortgage. It’s convenient, yes—but it’s rarely the smartest move. Most Canadians just sign and assume their renewal is set. The truth? A better rate or term could be just a quick check away. It literally takes less than a day to see if you can save hundreds—or even thousands—on your next term. Before you hit “sign,” get a second opinion. DM me and I’ll review your renewal quickly—no hassle, no stress. #mortgagerenewal #mortgagetips #canadianmortgage #homeownercanada #mortgagesavings

Most homeowners aren’t ready for what’s about to hit their monthly payments… If your mortgage was locked in around 2–3% during the pandemic, your renewal could look VERY different. Rates today are significantly higher—and that gap can mean hundreds or even thousands more every single month. And this isn’t a small group… millions of Canadians are set to renew over the next 24 months. Here’s the mistake most people make: They accept their lender’s first offer without exploring better options. What you should be doing instead: • Shop your renewal early (don’t wait for the letter) • Look at restructuring your amortization • Compare fixed vs variable based on your timeline—not fear • Use equity strategically to reduce monthly pressure The difference between a rushed renewal and a smart strategy could literally save you tens of thousands. Comment “RENEWAL” and I’ll show you how to minimize the payment shock before it hits. #mortgagerenewal #canadianmortgage #mortgagetips #homeownercanada #realestatecanada
